summary: Multi-system MWB key failure remains unclassified; attachment does not confirm the known signer rejection.

judgment.rationale: Three Windows 10 systems reportedly cannot use the old key or generate a new one after updating. The ZIP was inspected; relevant MWB logs show startup/service-path information but no untrusted-signature or SettingsSync rejection, so #50795 is not a proven cause.
evidence: Body reports v0.102.3001 across three Windows 10 Pro 22H2 systems; old key rejected and new key generation fails after update, even after config reset.
Inspected attached ZIP; relevant MWB log scan did not find untrusted-signature or Rejected SettingsSync.
Open #50795 covers a related same-release defect, but this issue has not established that exact error. No linked PR found.

information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reproduce one New key attempt and one old-key acceptance attempt on one affected PC, then comment `/bugreport` immediately afterward; include service/user mode and exact message.

comment.body: Thanks for confirming the failure across three Windows 10 systems and that resetting configuration did not help. I inspected the attached report, but its MWB logs do not show the first error needed to confirm the signer rejection tracked in #50795. Please reproduce one New key attempt and one old-key acceptance attempt on a single affected PC, then comment `/bugreport` immediately afterward; include whether MWB runs as service or user and the exact message. This distinguishes the known IPC failure from a different key/service path.
